subject: paediatrics
title: Measles, Koplik Spots, SSPE and Common Pediatric Exanthems

steps.tx: Childhood viral exanthems present with characteristic incubation periods, prodromal features, and rash morphology. The paramyxovirus infection **measles rubeola** is among the most contagious human pathogens, transmitted through aerosolized respiratory droplets with a secondary attack rate exceeding ninety percent in non-immune contacts. After a ten to fourteen-day incubation period, patients enter a dramatic three to four-day prodromal phase characterized by escalating fever and prominent mucosal inflammation.
steps.say: Measles is an airborne paramyxovirus with a secondary attack rate exceeding ninety percent. After a ten to fourteen-day incubation, patients develop severe prodromal fever and mucosal inflammation.

vis.caption: Measles viral pathogenesis, syncytial Warthin-Finkeldey giant cells, and craniocaudal rash progression. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The catarrhal prodrome features a classic triad of respiratory and ocular inflammatory signs. Patients exhibit high fever, brassy barking cough, profuse coryza, and prominent conjunctivitis with marked photophobia and lacrimation, clinically designated as the **three Cs of measles**. One to two days prior to the cutaneous rash, examination of the oral cavity reveals pathognomonic mucosal lesions that definitively establish early diagnosis.
steps.say: The measles prodrome features the three Cs: cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis with photophobia. Pathognomonic oral lesions appear one to two days before the cutaneous rash.

vis.alt: Oral mucosal view demonstrating pathognomonic Koplik spots opposite the second lower molars.
vis.caption: Koplik spots on buccal mucosa showing tiny bluish-white speckles on an erythematous base opposite lower molars. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Careful inspection of the buccal mucosa reveals the pathognomonic enanthem of wild measles infection. Known as **Koplik spots**, these lesions appear as tiny, bluish-white granular speckles surrounded by bright red erythematous areolae situated on the inner buccal mucosa opposite the lower second molars, resembling grains of salt. They appear roughly forty-eight hours before the skin rash, peak at exanthem onset, and vanish within two days.
steps.say: Koplik spots are pathognomonic tiny white grains on an erythematous base opposite the lower molars. They precede the skin eruption by two days and disappear as the rash matures.

left.title: Koplik Spots (Measles Enanthem)
points: Tiny bluish-white speckles opposite lower 2nd molars
Appears 1 to 2 days before cutaneous exanthem

right.title: Forchheimer Spots (Rubella Enanthem)
points: Located on soft palate and uvula
Not pathognomonic; occurs in measles and scarlet fever

steps.tx: The cutaneous eruption spreads across anatomical regions in a predictable temporal wave. The **craniocaudal maculopapular rash** of measles emerges on the fourth day of illness along the hairline, behind the mastoid ears, and across the upper neck. Over the next seventy-two hours, the erythematous macules coalesce and descend over the face, trunk, and extremities, ultimately fading in identical sequence leaving brownish hyperpigmentation and branny desquamation.
steps.say: The measles rash begins behind the ears on Day 4, coalescing and spreading downwards over the face, trunk, and limbs. It fades leaving fine branny desquamation and copper staining.

vis.alt: Clinical illustrations comparing rash appearance across pediatric exanthematous fevers.
vis.caption: Pediatric exanthematous rashes compared by day of appearance, distribution pattern, and morphology. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: High-dose retinoid therapy significantly reduces secondary bacterial pneumonia and overall mortality. The World Health Organization mandates **therapeutic vitamin A in measles**, administering two consecutive daily oral doses of 200,000 international units for children aged twelve months or older, 100,000 units for infants aged six to eleven months, and 50,000 units for younger infants. Retinol restores respiratory epithelial integrity and prevents post-measles keratomalacia, halving mortality.
steps.say: Give two daily high doses of vitamin A to all children with measles regardless of nutritional state. Vitamin A preserves respiratory epithelium and reduces mortality by fifty percent.

steps.tx: Persistent mutant viral replication within central neurones produces a fatal late neurodegenerative complication. The catastrophic sequela **subacute sclerosing panencephalitis** (SSPE) develops seven to ten years after wild measles infection, especially when acquired before two years of age. Patients experience insidious cognitive decline, school failure, personality changes, progressive myoclonic jerks synchronized with periodic burst complexes on electroencephalograms, and dementia, terminating fatally within one to three years.
steps.say: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis is a fatal late demyelinating disease striking years after infant measles. It causes progressive dementia, myoclonic jerks with periodic EEG bursts, and death.

vis.alt: Pathology of SSPE showing cortical demyelination, viral inclusions, and periodic EEG burst patterns.
vis.caption: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis pathology showing neuronal viral inclusions and periodic synchronous EEG complexes. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Mild togaviral infection poses severe teratogenic risks during maternal gestational transmission. Known as German measles, **rubella viral exanthem** produces a mild three-day pink maculopapular rash accompanied by tender suboccipital and postauricular lymphadenopathy and Forchheimer petechial palatal spots. However, maternal gestational rubella provokes congenital rubella syndrome, classically featuring the Gregg triad: sensorineural deafness, microphthalmia with cataracts, and patent ductus arteriosus.
steps.say: Rubella causes a mild three-day rash with tender postauricular lymph nodes. Maternal infection during pregnancy triggers congenital rubella syndrome, causing deafness, cataracts, and patent ductus arteriosus.

steps.tx: Rapidly evolving pleomorphic crops across different developmental stages define human herpesvirus 3 infection. In **varicella chickenpox**, pruritic teardrop vesicles on erythematous bases (dew drops on a rose petal) appear in centripetal crops over the trunk and face. At any given moment, macules, papules, clear vesicles, pustules, and crusted scabs coexist simultaneously, distinguishing varicella from smallpox where all lesions remain in a uniform single developmental stage.
steps.say: Varicella presents with dew-drop vesicles on red bases, spreading centripetally. Simultaneous crops of macules, vesicles, and crusted scabs distinguish chickenpox from smallpox.
